          Man City's Resilience, Lyon Dominate, Questions for Chelsea & Arsenal: UWCL Matchday 1 Lessons
        
      
                          
                      Sep 24, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Yash Thakur / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Matchday 1 of the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League delivered drama, dominant displays and plenty of talking points. We dive into the data to analyse the key stories from the action.
The 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League is underway and Matchday 1 delivered a little bit of everything.
There were narrow wins, thrashings and end-to-end contests as Europe's elite began their quest for continental glory.
Using Opta data, we break down the standout performers and biggest talking points from the opening matchday of this season's UWCL.
The reigning WSL champions began their UWCL campaign with one of the toughest assignments possible, travelling to Munich to face a Bayern side ranked second in the Opta Power Rankings.
The contest delivered everything expected of two European heavyweights: goals, a missed penalty and late drama, with the points ultimately shared in a 2-2 draw.
In doing so, City became the first English side to avoid defeat at Bayern Munich in the UWCL.

It was the first time in City’s history in the competition they had avoided defeat when trailing by two or more goals, while it was just the second time Bayern had failed to win a UWCL game in which they had led by 2+ goals, last doing so against Roma in November 2023.
José Barcala's team asserted themselves early, racing into a two-goal lead before the break. Their aggressive pressing forced City into mistakes, with Bayern recording 16 high turnovers.
Since 2019-20, only against Barcelona in December 2024 (25) and March 2021 (17) have City conceded more high turnovers in the competition.
City struggled to gain a foothold before half-time, managing only three attempts. But Beth Mead's goal shifted the momentum after the interval.

The visitors were then handed a golden opportunity to level from the penalty spot, only forEna Mahmutovic to brilliantly deny Khadija Shaw. It was the first penalty Shaw has missed since joining Manchester City.

Despite that setback, City continued to push and their persistence was rewarded in the 86th minute when Carlotta Wamser found the equaliser to complete the comeback with her first goal in light blue, and secure a valuable point on the road.
Andrée Jeglertz's influence from the bench again proved significant, as had been the case against Liverpool.

Second-half substitute Laura Blindkilde Brown provided the assist for Wamser's goal and helped City gain greater control in possession, offering composure against Bayern's intense press as the visitors finished the stronger of the two sides.
Arsenal and Chelsea both opened their European campaigns with 1-0 victories against HB Køge and Austria Wien respectively, but neither performance fully convinced.
With a heavyweight WSL meeting at Stamford Bridge looming this weekend, both sides left MD1 with three points, but just as many questions remain.
Arsenal needed a stoppage-time Mariona Caldentey penalty to overcome Danish champions Køge in a game they largely controlled but struggled to break open.
Renée Slegers' side monopolised possession, recording 69.7% of the ball and completing 620 passes at an 86% success rate, but their dominance rarely translated into clear-cut opportunities.

Despite attempting 19 shots, Arsenal generated only one big chance and managed just a single effort on target prior to Caldentey's winning penalty. It was another example of a recurring issue for the Gunners: controlling games without creating enough high-quality chances.
